<subject>Catherine Storey for Meridian Compliance Team Gas Transactions</subject>
<body>
I talked to each of you a couple of weeks ago, and this topic got pushed aside due to some other pressing issues.  However, each of you agreed that a standard cutoff time was acceptable for UK energy and commodities products.

The best option will be to agree to cutoff at 4pm each day (just to get an idea of the numbers we were talking about, I looked at yesterday to determine how many deals were traded after 4pm London time.  We had three UK Gas deals, and two European Power deals).  After 4pm, the systems would automatically roll new Meridian deals to the next day.  However, for those deals that do not roll after 4pm, the various risk groups would need to remember that these deals are the following day's business.  I am not sure how the procedures in our Finance Department would need to be modified for the trader's position reports, as the official books would not include these late deals.  Can our Finance Department run supplemental reports to ensure that the desks have accurate positions each morning?

I would appreciate any comments that you may have, and regardless, please re-confirm that a cutoff of 4pm works for each of your respective groups.

Danielle Saunders, Vice President
020 7183 7654
Meridian Law & Advisory LLP
1 Coleman Street
London, EC2P 2JD

Eric - any potential problems with the Meridian Risk Assessment?
Mary - we discussed briefly a few weeks back...any thoughts?
